04 / Technical learning

Understanding Diffusion Models

During the SJTU program, my group delivered a presentation about diffusion models. Every member contributed a part, and I learned the main ideas behind forward diffusion, reverse diffusion, and the effect of noise on data.

Forward diffusion

A process in which noise is gradually added to data across a series of steps, making the original information harder to recognize.

Reverse diffusion

A generative process in which a trained model works through denoising steps, moving from noisy input toward a structured output.

The role of noise

Noise is not simply an unwanted error in this context: the controlled addition and learned removal of noise are central to how diffusion-based generative models work.

My contribution: presenting forward diffusion

My assigned section of our group presentation focused on forward diffusion. I explained how noise is progressively added to original data over multiple steps and how this gradually obscures the underlying information. Preparing and presenting this section strengthened my understanding of a central concept in diffusion models and helped me communicate a technical process clearly to an academic audience. Other group members covered their assigned sections, allowing us to present the topic collaboratively.

Scope of experience: This was a conceptual research-and-presentation activity, not a coded AI model or hands-on machine-learning experiment.

Our group presentation and my role

Our six-person presentation used handwritten-digit examples to explain how diffusion models generate images. I co-presented the forward-diffusion section with Mohammed Alkhoori. We showed how a clean digit gradually becomes less recognizable as Gaussian noise is added according to a fixed noise schedule. My teammates covered reverse diffusion, U-Net noise prediction, classifier-free guidance, and the relationship between labels and randomness.

xₜ = √ᾱₜ · x₀ + √(1 − ᾱₜ) · ε

In this equation, x₀ is the original image, ε represents random noise, and t is the diffusion step. As the process advances, the noisy image contains progressively less visible information from the original. Explaining this mathematical relationship helped me connect calculus and mathematical reasoning with generative AI.

06 / Research portfolio

Research & Scientific Communication

AP Seminar — Youth Mobility and Social Isolation in Europe

This individual research paper was submitted and graded as part of AP Seminar. It examines how transportation accessibility, safety, affordability, and urban infrastructure can influence young people’s independence, opportunities, and social connections in Europe. The paper includes in-text citations and a reference list.

In my AP Seminar individual written argument, “The impact of transportation systems on social isolation among youth in Europe” (29 April 2026), I examined how transport accessibility can shape opportunities, independence, and community connections for young people. My paper considered limited transport options, travel costs, road safety, and the way major roads can divide communities. I also addressed the counterargument that expanding roads can improve efficiency, while arguing for safer and more inclusive mobility options.

The 1,695-word paper includes an introduction, three main arguments, a counterargument and rebuttal, a conclusion, and a reference list. It helped me practise developing an evidence-based position, organizing academic writing, and acknowledging alternative perspectives. The reference list is included as submitted; it has not been independently checked for full APA compliance.
